claim: Under VOC rule in Ceylon, cinnamon production relied substantially on corvée obligations assigned to chialia/chalea groups, who were required to harvest and deliver cinnamon for the Company; these burdens generated recurrent resistance and flight.
bounded_by: The relationship between caste identity, pre-colonial service obligations and VOC reorganisation is historically layered. This claim establishes VOC use and intensification of corvée, not that the Company invented the social category ex nihilo. Ekama's discussion of the 1661 ordinance supports Company regulation of marriage/child placement used to prevent cinnamon peelers escaping caste duties, but the underlying Hovy edition should be consulted directly before primary-source quotation.
notes: RUN44 adds a corroborating labour-law anchor to the RUN41 bounded proposition.
